docs.title: Vector AI Engineering template (uv edition) repository
docs.text:
This template repository can be used to bootstrap AI Engineering project repositories on Github! The template is meant for python codebases since Python is the most commonly used language by our team.

The template includes:

  • pyproject.toml file to specify repository information and manage dependencies using uv.

  • README.md which should have basic information on why the project is useful, installation instructions and other information on how users can get started.

  • .pre-commit-config.yaml for running pre-commit hooks that check for code-style, apply formatting, check for type hints and run tests.

  • .github/pull_request_template.md for PRs.

  • .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE for bug reports and issues that can be raised on the repository.

  • .github/workflows for running CI workflows using Github actions. The template includes CI workflows for code checks, documentation building and releasing python packages to PyPI.

  • LICENSE.md for adding a license to the project repository. By default, this is the Apache-2.0 license. Please change according to your project!

  • docs for adding project documentation. Typically projects should have API reference documentation, user guides and tutorials.

  • CONTRIBUTING.md with basic guidelines on how others can contribute to the repository.

  • CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md with standards on how the community engages in a healthy and constructive manner.

  • .gitignore with some standard file extensions to be ignored by git. Please add/modify as necessary.

  • codecov.yml for using codecov.io to generate code coverage information for your repository. You would need to add codecov.io app as an integration to your repository.

If you are starting a new project, you can navigate to the Use this template button on the top right corner of the template repository home page which will allow you to bootstrap your project repo using this template.

Please check out the user guide page for more detailed information on using the template features. For existing projects, the user guide can be followed to migrate to following the template more closely.

docs.title: Architecture & Design Decisions
docs.text:
• Preempt-Guardrail removes AGE, MONEY, and NAME from the user prompt before the LLM call. Usage example: src/preempt/demo.ipynb.
  • Training, NER evaluation, and the end-to-end benchmark stay on separate branches off main, each with its own uv group:
  • feat/training (train) — fine-tune the DistilBERT NER for NAME, AGE, MONEY.
  • feat/ner-bench (ner-bench) — detection accuracy, quantization, and latency.
  • feat/pii-bench (pii-bench) — utility and privacy across ε, verifiable tasks, and an LLM judge.
  • The default install runs an exported ONNX graph. DistilBertRecognizer defaults to PyTorch and needs the torch extra. Pass backend="onnx" on a default install. GLiNER and checkpoint export are the gliner and export extras.
  • Benchmark data is synthetic. Keep real personal data, including public chat corpora, out of ground-truth metrics. A later sanity-check corpus needs a license check and a separate PII relabel.
  • Scored detection set: 36 templates × 10 fills = 360 prompts in data/dataset.jsonl. 240 are incidental (email drafts, general explanations). 120 are verifiable (retirement, age gates, savings rate, raise). Recognizer and sanitizer ran on all 360 at ε = 1 via metrics.detection.
  • Values this round generates: integer ages; money as $12,000, $12k, or 12,000 dollars.
  • Partial recall uses IoU ≥ 0.5. Per-item rows are in runs/detection_validation.jsonl. Strict money F1 is 0.40 because the recognizer labels the digits inside $12,000 while the gold span includes $. Partial money F1 is 0.83. Quote the partial figure for money detection.
  • Sanitizer(ner_model, key, tweak) has no default key. The name permutation and FF3 money cipher are seeded only by key:tweak, so a published default would let anyone reverse surrogates. Use preempt.generate_key() for a fresh pair. Library tests pass a fixed key. feat/pii-bench still calls Sanitizer with no key and needs the same change; this branch does not contain that code.
  • Sanitizer accepts a Recognizer directly and wraps it in LegacyNERShim. preempt/__init__.py re-exports Sanitizer, generate_key, LegacyNERShim, and the contracts, but not the recognizers, which load transformers or the gliner extra.
  • demo.ipynb reads PREEMPT_MODEL_PATH, PREEMPT_KEY, and PREEMPT_TWEAK (see .env.example) and loads model.onnx, not the int8 graph. Re-execute it with uv run --env-file .env --with nbconvert --with ipywidgets jupyter nbconvert --execute --inplace src/preempt/demo.ipynb. Without ipywidgets a tqdm warning writes a local path into the outputs. The kernel cannot start inside the agent sandbox.
  • Compare configurations with a paired bootstrap on per-prompt means. Claim a difference only when the confidence interval excludes zero.
  • The generator model and the judge model must be from different families.
  • Offline CI path: MockSanitizer plus a stub LLM, 10 items, under 60 seconds. Seed the dataset, each sanitizer draw, and the bootstrap. Content-address the LLM cache and store model name and version on every record. Log full prompts; keep them off CI stdout.
  • Bench tests that must exist before a run is trusted: slot spans, normalized leakage (85k / 85,000 / eighty-five thousand), name rehydration (possessives, case, partial names), FINAL_ANSWER parsing, each answer_fn, threshold distance, bootstrap CIs, judge JSON schema, and a golden file of the rendered judge prompt.

docs.title: Gotchas & Edge Cases
docs.text:
• 12,000 dollars is the money format NER misses: 15/119 found (failure 0.87). $12,000 is 107/107 and $12k is 134/134.
  • Integer ages: 201/210 found (failure 0.04). Full names: 408/470 found (failure 0.13).
  • After sanitization at ε = 1, an original value remains in 145/360 prompts (0.40). Money accounts for 117/360 prompts; names account for 64/470 name spans. Those denominators differ — prompts versus spans.
  • Look-alikes (metrics.lookalikes, 20 non-record lines): 3 spans, all NAME — "Jordan" as a destination, "Jordan" as a person asked for notes, and "Bill". Left untagged: Apple, "the bill for dinner", Mark 4:12, version 52, Route 66, iPhone 15, "the age of the universe", China, Turkey, Georgia.
  • The PII-masking train download (110,790 conversation rows, 54 label types, about 85 MB) lives in training-data/, which .gitignore excludes. Nothing in this branch reads it. A fresh clone does not have it, and it sits outside src/preempt, so it cannot land in the wheel.
  • On model.onnx (run 407944) the demo sentence "Ben Parker and John Doe" yields Ben Parker and misses John Doe, so "John Doe" is left in place. The same graph does detect Hamid Aziz and Jose Santiago in the longer passage, and those round-trip. FPE money loses thousands separators ($10,000 is sanitized with no comma and decrypts to $10000).
  • Long text is scanned in overlapping windows (DistilBertRecognizer.stride, default 128 content tokens; GlinerRecognizer.overlap, default 32 words). tokenizers return_overflowing_tokens only returns one extra chunk, so the windows are built from the untruncated offsets. An entity longer than the overlap can still be split. If a long text has no character offsets, recognition raises instead of returning a silent prefix.
  • One value FF3 or the parser cannot encrypt is replaced with [REDACTED] (preempt.sanitizer.REDACTED). The row is still listed in invalid, and the other values in that text are still replaced. FF3 money appends 999999 (MONEY_FPE_SUFFIX) rather than prefixing it: a prefix made the right half of a round amount ($1,000,000) all zeros, and pyfpe raises ValueError: string 000000 is not within base/radix. Decrypt strips that suffix.
  • decrypt restores only surrogates saved by the last encrypt on that instance. A name the recognizer missed, or an amount the model reply added, is left as written. key_only=True is the explicit path that inverts listed names and FPE amounts with the key alone. In that mode an amount FF3 rejects is skipped, so one value cannot fail the batch. use_cache is still accepted and does not change this. Ages stay stateful either way.
  • Leave ordinary look-alikes alone this round. A later hard-negative slice is place names that are also given names.
  • Unsupported, so absent from the dataset: ages as words, birth dates, birth years, decades ("early 50s"), relative ages ("I'll be 60 next month"); money as words, slang ("about 85 grand"), ranges, or relations ("2x my spouse's salary").
  • runs/sweep-v2/ is the earlier 90-prompt sweep. It is a different run from the 360-prompt detection pass.

docs.title: Tooling & Environment Quirks
docs.text:
• Package manager is uv. The environment is .venv at the repo root. Layout is src, which differs from Poetry's flat layout.
  • typos splits on hyphens, so look-alikes is reported as alikes. Mata in demo.ipynb is a generated surname. Both are allowlisted in typos.toml under extend-ignore-words-re. A new notebook run can introduce another surname that the checker rejects.
  • uv sync installs the ONNX runtime. An exported ONNX file runs without PyTorch or Optimum.
  • pyfpe 0.10.3 requires pycryptodome==3.10.1. pip-audit flags that release (PYSEC-2026-1811, fixed in 3.19.1). tool.uv.override-dependencies lifts it. The FF3 round-trip tests pass on pycryptodome 4.x.
  • Extras: uv sync --extra torch, --extra gliner, --extra export.
  • Dev and test dependencies: uv sync --dev. Drop a group with uv sync --no-group docs.
  • Branch stacks, checked out on that branch: uv sync --group train, --group ner-bench, or --group pii-bench.

docs.title: Active & Pending Technical Debt
docs.text:
• Resolve before Milestone 8, when the real sanitizer is wired:
  • Sanitizer transport (Python function, REST, or CLI), and whether it returns the substitution map and spans.
  • ε range and parameterization, and the distance metric mLDP uses.
  • Which generator and judge models to use (different families).
  • Whether FPE name mapping preserves gender, culture, and length. That answer decides whether to add pronoun-consistency checks.
  • Whether this round includes non-English prompts.
  • Still unrun on the 360-prompt set: generator, judge, a full ε sweep, privacy attacks, human labels for the judge, bootstrap intervals, and per-type ablations.
  • Open quality gaps from the ε = 1 detection pass: N dollars recognition (failure 0.87) and residual original values in 0.40 of prompts. Strict versus partial money spans still disagree on the $.
  • Large runs need a dry-run cost estimate and a confirmation prompt. Pilot is 50 items, 2 ε values, k = 2, and that report is reviewed before the full run.
  • Milestones 1–3 come first. Stop for review before spending LLM budget on the full run.

class LegacyNERShim:
    """Presents a Recognizer as ``NER.extract`` for Name, Money, and Age."""

    def __init__(self, recognizer: Recognizer) -> None:
        """Store the recognizer used for extract().

        Parameters
        ----------
        recognizer : Recognizer
            Span recognizer to adapt.

        """
        self.recognizer = recognizer

    def extract(
        self,
        prompts: list[str],
        entity_type: str,
        batch_size: int = 1,
        output_dict: dict[str, list[list[str]]] | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, list[list[str]]]:
        """Return surface strings for one sanitizer entity type.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompts : list[str]
            Input texts, one string per row.
        entity_type : str
            ``Name``, ``Money``, or ``Age``.
        batch_size : int
            Unused. Accepted so the call matches ``NER.extract``.
        output_dict : dict[str, list[list[str]]] | None
            Existing dictionary to update.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[list[str]]]
            ``{entity_type: [[span text, ...], ...]}``, one list per prompt.
            Adjacent ``Name`` spans separated only by whitespace are one string.

        """
        del batch_size
        try:
            label = SANITIZER_ENTITY[entity_type]
        except KeyError:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported entity type: {entity_type}") from None
        if output_dict is None:
            output_dict = {}
        result = []
        for prompt in prompts:
            spans = [span for span in self.recognizer.recognize(prompt) if span.label == label]
            extracted_texts = [span.text for span in spans]
            if entity_type == "Name":
                extracted_texts = join_name_spans(prompt, spans)
            result.append(extracted_texts)
        output_dict[entity_type] = result

        return output_dict

Encrypt and decrypt names, money, and ages detected by ner_model.

Source code in src/preempt/sanitizer.py 
class Sanitizer:
    """Encrypt and decrypt names, money, and ages detected by ``ner_model``."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        ner_model: Any,
        key: str,
        tweak: str,
        seed: Optional[int] = None,
    ):
        """Set up the FF3 cipher and name permutations for ``key`` and ``tweak``.

        Anyone with ``key`` and ``tweak`` can reverse FPE names and amounts,
        so keep them secret. Use ``generate_key`` to make a fresh pair.
        ``ner_model`` is either an object with ``extract`` or a ``Recognizer``,
        which is wrapped in ``LegacyNERShim``.
        """
        self.cipher_fn = FF3Cipher(key, tweak, allow_small_domain=True, radix=10)
        self._key, self._tweak = key, tweak
        if hasattr(ner_model, "recognize") and not hasattr(ner_model, "extract"):
            ner_model = LegacyNERShim(ner_model)
        self.ner = ner_model
        # Set by encrypt(), read by decrypt().
        self.entity_mapping: list[dict[str, Optional[str]]] = []  # {original: fake} per text
        # {fake word: original word} per text, for name words outside the fixed lists.
        self.entity_lookup: list[dict[str, str]] = []
        self._names_dataset: Optional[dict[str, list[str]]] = None
        self._name_lists: dict[str, list[str]] = {}  # {"first" | "last": names}
        self._name_index: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
        self._name_perm: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        self._name_inverse: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        self.reseed(seed)

    def reseed(self, seed: Optional[int]) -> None:
        """Reset the RNGs used by m-LDP noise and random names."""
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        if seed is not None:
            random.seed(seed)

    # --- Public API -----------------------------------------------------------

    def encrypt(
        self, inputs: list[str], epsilon: float = 0.1, entity: str = "Name", use_mdp: bool = False, use_fpe: bool = True
    ) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:
        """Replace every detected ``entity`` ("Name", "Money", or "Age") in ``inputs``.

        A value that cannot be encrypted is replaced with ``[REDACTED]`` and its
        row index is returned in the second list. Other values in that row are
        still replaced.
        """
        extracted = self.ner.extract(inputs, entity_type=entity)[entity]
        if entity == "Name":
            self.entity_mapping, self.entity_lookup = self.encrypt_names(extracted, use_fpe=use_fpe)
        elif entity == "Money":
            if not (use_fpe or use_mdp):
                raise ValueError("Money needs use_fpe or use_mdp to be True.")
            self.entity_mapping = self.encrypt_money(extracted, use_fpe=use_fpe, epsilon=epsilon)
        elif entity == "Age":
            self.entity_mapping = self.encrypt_age(extracted, epsilon=epsilon)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown entity: {entity!r}")

        sanitized, invalid = [], []
        for i, (line, fakes) in enumerate(zip(inputs, self.entity_mapping)):
            replaced = line
            failed = False
            for original, fake in fakes.items():
                if fake is None:
                    failed = True
                    replaced = _nfc(replaced).replace(_nfc(original), REDACTED)
                    continue
                replaced = _nfc(replaced).replace(_nfc(original), fake)
            if failed:
                invalid.append(i)
            sanitized.append(replaced)
        return sanitized, invalid

    def decrypt(  # noqa: PLR0917
        self,
        inputs: list[str],
        entity: str = "Name",
        extracted: Optional[list[list[str]]] = None,
        use_mdp: bool = False,  # noqa: ARG002 -- kept for API compatibility; m-LDP is used when not use_fpe
        use_fpe: bool = True,
        use_cache: bool = False,  # noqa: ARG002 -- stateful decrypt always uses saved surrogates
        key_only: bool = False,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Restore values that ``encrypt`` replaced.

        By default only surrogates saved by the last ``encrypt`` call on this
        instance are restored. A name or amount that was never encrypted is
        left as it is, including one the recognizer missed and one added later.

        Pass ``key_only=True`` to invert listed names and FPE amounts with the
        key alone. Targets then come from ``extracted``, or from a fresh
        recognizer pass when ``extracted`` is omitted. An amount FF3 rejects
        is left in place. Ages have no key-only inverse; they still use the
        saved state.

        ``use_cache`` is accepted for existing callers. Stateful decrypt always
        uses the saved surrogates.
        """
        if key_only and extracted is None and entity != "Age":
            extracted = self.ner.extract(inputs, entity_type=entity)[entity]
        if entity == "Name":
            return self.decrypt_names(inputs, extracted, key_only=key_only)
        if entity == "Money":
            return self.decrypt_money(inputs, extracted, use_fpe=use_fpe, key_only=key_only)
        if entity == "Age":
            return self.decrypt_age(inputs)
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown entity: {entity!r}")

    # --- Names ----------------------------------------------------------------

    def encrypt_names(
        self, inputs: list[list[str]], use_fpe: bool = True
    ) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Optional[str]]], list[dict[str, str]]]:
        """Map each name to a fake name, per text.

        With FPE, each word is swapped on its own (first word in the first-name
        list, later words in the last-name list), so "Sarah Lopez", "Sarah" and
        "Lopez" map consistently, within and across calls. Without FPE, fake
        names are random and can't be decrypted.

        Returns ``{original: fake}`` per text and, per text, the
        ``{fake word: original word}`` entries for words outside the lists.
        """
        if not use_fpe:
            mappings: list[dict[str, Optional[str]]] = []
            for text_names in inputs:
                fakes: dict[str, Optional[str]] = {}
                for name in text_names:
                    fakes.setdefault(name, names.get_full_name(gender="male"))
                mappings.append(fakes)
            return mappings, [{} for _ in inputs]

        self._load_name_lists()
        mappings, fallbacks = [], []
        for text_names in inputs:
            roles = self._word_roles(text_names)
            word_fakes = {w: self._permute_word(w, role) for w, role in roles.items() if w in self._name_index[role]}
            # Unlisted words get a keyed pick that avoids surrogates used here.
            used = set(word_fakes.values())
            fallback: dict[str, str] = {}
            for word, role in roles.items():
                if word not in word_fakes:
                    fake = self._fallback_word(word, role, used)
                    word_fakes[word] = fake
                    fallback[fake] = word
                    used.add(fake)

            fakes = {}
            for name in text_names:
                fakes.setdefault(name, " ".join(word_fakes[w] for w in _nfc(name).split()))
            for word, fake in word_fakes.items():
                fakes.setdefault(word, fake)
            mappings.append(fakes)
            fallbacks.append(fallback)
        return mappings, fallbacks

    def decrypt_names(
        self,
        inputs: list[str],
        extracted: Optional[list[list[str]]],
        use_cache: bool = False,  # noqa: ARG002 -- stateful decrypt always uses saved surrogates
        key_only: bool = False,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Replace fake names in ``inputs`` with the originals.

        By default only surrogates from the last ``encrypt`` call are undone.
        ``key_only=True`` inverts every target with the key. Words from the
        fixed lists need only the key; words that were outside the lists need
        the state saved by ``encrypt``. Words that are neither are left as
        they are.
        """
        self._load_name_lists()
        decrypted = []
        for i, line in enumerate(inputs):
            fallback = self.entity_lookup[i] if i < len(self.entity_lookup) else {}
            restored = line
            for fake in self._decrypt_targets(i, extracted, key_only):
                restored = restored.replace(fake, self._decrypt_name(fake, fallback))
            decrypted.append(restored)
        return decrypted

    def _decrypt_name(self, fake: str, fallback: dict[str, str]) -> str:
        """Undo the word swaps in one fake name."""
        words = _nfc(fake).split()
        if len(words) == 1:
            # The lists share no names, so a lone word's list is unambiguous.
            roles = ["first" if words[0] in self._name_index["first"] else "last"]
        else:
            roles = ["first"] + ["last"] * (len(words) - 1)
        restored = []
        for word, role in zip(words, roles):
            if word in fallback:
                restored.append(fallback[word])
            elif (i := self._name_index[role].get(word)) is not None:
                restored.append(self._name_lists[role][self._name_inverse[role][i]])
            else:
                restored.append(word)
        return " ".join(restored)

    def _word_roles(self, text_names: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Assign each name word to the "first" or "last" list, once per text."""
        later_words = {w for name in text_names for w in _nfc(name).split()[1:]}
        roles: dict[str, str] = {}
        for name in text_names:
            words = _nfc(name).split()
            for pos, word in enumerate(words):
                if word in roles:
                    continue
                if len(words) > 1:
                    roles[word] = "first" if pos == 0 else "last"
                elif word in later_words or (
                    word in self._name_index["last"] and word not in self._name_index["first"]
                ):
                    roles[word] = "last"
                else:
                    roles[word] = "first"
        return roles

    def _permute_word(self, word: str, role: str) -> str:
        return self._name_lists[role][self._name_perm[role][self._name_index[role][word]]]

    def _fallback_word(self, word: str, role: str, used: set[str]) -> str:
        """Pick a list name for an unlisted word by keyed hash, skipping ``used``."""
        names_list = self._name_lists[role]
        for attempt in itertools.count():
            digest = hashlib.sha256(f"{self._key}:{self._tweak}:{role}:{word}:{attempt}".encode()).digest()
            fake = names_list[int.from_bytes(digest[:8], "big") % len(names_list)]
            if fake not in used:
                return fake
        raise AssertionError("unreachable")

    def _load_name_lists(self) -> None:
        """Build the fixed first/last name lists and their keyed permutations once.

        The lists depend only on the names dataset, never on the inputs, so a
        name's surrogate depends only on the name and the key. The last-name
        list excludes every first name, so the two lists share no names.
        """
        if self._name_lists:
            return
        dataset = self._load_names_dataset()
        first = _clean_names(dataset["first_names"], exclude=set())
        last = _clean_names(dataset["last_names"], exclude=set(first))
        if len(first) < ALPHABET_SIZE or len(last) < ALPHABET_SIZE:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Names dataset has {len(first)} first and {len(last)} last names; need {ALPHABET_SIZE} of each."
            )
        for role, names_list in (("first", first[:ALPHABET_SIZE]), ("last", last[:ALPHABET_SIZE])):
            seed = int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(f"{self._key}:{self._tweak}:{role}".encode()).digest()[:8], "big")
            perm = np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation(ALPHABET_SIZE)
            self._name_lists[role] = names_list
            self._name_index[role] = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(names_list)}
            self._name_perm[role] = perm
            self._name_inverse[role] = np.argsort(perm)

    def _load_names_dataset(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """Load the dataset of first and last names once, generating it if missing."""
        if self._names_dataset is not None:
            return self._names_dataset
        candidates = [
            os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "names_dataset.json"),
            "preempt/names_dataset.json",
            f"{os.getcwd()}/names_dataset.json",
        ]
        path = next((p for p in candidates if os.path.exists(p)), None)
        if path is None:
            path = candidates[-1]
            logger.info("Names dataset not found. Generating %s", path)
            make_names_dataset(path)
        self._names_dataset = load_data(path)
        return self._names_dataset

    # --- Money ----------------------------------------------------------------

    def encrypt_money(
        self, inputs: list[list[str]], use_fpe: bool = True, epsilon: Optional[float] = None
    ) -> list[dict[str, Optional[str]]]:
        """Map each amount to an FPE-encrypted or m-LDP-noised amount, per text.

        Amounts that can't be parsed map to None.
        """
        mappings = []
        for amounts in inputs:
            fakes: dict[str, Optional[str]] = {}
            for amount in amounts:
                if amount in fakes:
                    continue
                digits = amount.replace(",", "")
                try:
                    if use_fpe:
                        fakes[amount] = self.fpe_encrypt(digits + MONEY_FPE_SUFFIX)
                    else:
                        value = int(float(digits))
                        fakes[amount] = str(self.m_epsilon(value, *_money_bounds(value), epsilon))
                except (ValueError, TypeError):
                    fakes[amount] = None
            mappings.append(fakes)
        return mappings

    def decrypt_money(
        self,
        inputs: list[str],
        extracted: Optional[list[list[str]]],
        use_fpe: bool = True,
        use_cache: bool = False,  # noqa: ARG002 -- stateful decrypt always uses saved surrogates
        key_only: bool = False,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Replace fake amounts in ``inputs`` with the originals.

        By default only surrogates from the last ``encrypt`` call are undone.
        ``key_only=True`` inverts FPE amounts with the key and skips a value
        FF3 rejects, so one amount cannot fail the batch.
        """
        decrypted = []
        for i, line in enumerate(inputs):
            restored = line
            mapping = self.entity_mapping[i] if i < len(self.entity_mapping) else {}
            fake_to_original = {fake: original for original, fake in mapping.items() if fake is not None}
            for fake in self._decrypt_targets(i, extracted, key_only):
                if not use_fpe:
                    original = fake_to_original.get(fake)
                    if original is None:
                        continue
                    restored = _replace_first_word(restored, fake, original)
                    continue
                original = self._unwrap_money(fake)
                if original is None:
                    continue
                if fake in restored:
                    restored = restored.replace(fake, original)
                else:  # e.g. "1.250" was written as "1,250"
                    restored = restored.replace(fake.replace(".", ","), original.replace(".", ","))
            decrypted.append(restored)
        return decrypted

    # --- Age ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def encrypt_age(self, inputs: list[list[str]], epsilon: Optional[float] = None) -> list[dict[str, Optional[str]]]:
        """Map each age to an m-LDP-noised age in [10, 99], per text.

        Ages that can't be parsed map to None.
        """
        mappings = []
        for ages in inputs:
            fakes: dict[str, Optional[str]] = {}
            for age in ages:
                if age in fakes:
                    continue
                try:
                    fakes[age] = str(self.m_epsilon(int(age), 10, 99, epsilon))
                except (ValueError, TypeError):
                    fakes[age] = None
            mappings.append(fakes)
        return mappings

    def decrypt_age(self, inputs: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        """Restore ages saved by the last ``encrypt`` call."""
        decrypted = []
        for line, fakes in zip(inputs, self.entity_mapping):
            restored = line
            for original, fake in fakes.items():
                if fake is not None:
                    restored = _replace_first_word(restored, fake, original)
            decrypted.append(restored)
        return decrypted

    # --- Building blocks ------------------------------------------------------

    def fpe_encrypt(self, value: str) -> str:
        """FPE-encrypt the digits of ``value``, keeping its punctuation."""
        return _restore_format(self.cipher_fn.encrypt(_digits_only(value)), str(value))

    def fpe_decrypt(self, value: str) -> str:
        """Undo ``fpe_encrypt``."""
        return _restore_format(self.cipher_fn.decrypt(_digits_only(value)), str(value))

    def m_epsilon(self, x: int, n_lower: int, n_upper: int, epsilon: float, discretization_size: int = 100) -> int:
        """Noise ``x`` with m-LDP: sample near ``x`` within [n_lower, n_upper].

        Smaller ``epsilon`` means more noise.
        """
        n_lower, n_upper = int(n_lower), int(n_upper)
        total_range = n_upper - n_lower
        x_scaled = (x - n_lower) * discretization_size / total_range
        p = np.exp(-np.abs(x_scaled - np.arange(discretization_size)) * epsilon / 2)
        sample = self.rng.choice(discretization_size, 1, p=p / p.sum())[0]
        return int(sample * total_range / discretization_size + n_lower)

    def _unwrap_money(self, fake: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """Return the original digits of an FPE amount.

        ``None`` when ``fake`` is too short to be one of ours, FF3 rejects it,
        or decrypting it does not end in the suffix this class appends.
        """
        if len(_digits_only(fake)) <= len(MONEY_FPE_SUFFIX):
            return None
        try:
            decoded = self.fpe_decrypt(fake)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            return None
        if not decoded.endswith(MONEY_FPE_SUFFIX):
            return None
        return decoded[: -len(MONEY_FPE_SUFFIX)]

    def _saved_fakes(self, index: int) -> list[str]:
        """Surrogates saved by ``encrypt`` for text ``index``, in insertion order."""
        if index >= len(self.entity_mapping):
            return []
        return [fake for fake in dict.fromkeys(self.entity_mapping[index].values()) if fake is not None]

    def _decrypt_targets(self, index: int, extracted: Optional[list[list[str]]], key_only: bool) -> list[str]:
        """Values to undo in text ``index``.

        Stateful decrypt uses the surrogates ``encrypt`` saved. Key-only
        decrypt uses ``extracted`` and does not require that call.
        """
        if not key_only:
            return self._saved_fakes(index)
        if extracted is None:
            return []
        return list(extracted[index])

def __init__(
    self,
    ner_model: Any,
    key: str,
    tweak: str,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
):
    """Set up the FF3 cipher and name permutations for ``key`` and ``tweak``.

    Anyone with ``key`` and ``tweak`` can reverse FPE names and amounts,
    so keep them secret. Use ``generate_key`` to make a fresh pair.

def encrypt(
    self, inputs: list[str], epsilon: float = 0.1, entity: str = "Name", use_mdp: bool = False, use_fpe: bool = True
) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:
    """Replace every detected ``entity`` ("Name", "Money", or "Age") in ``inputs``.

    A value that cannot be encrypted is replaced with ``[REDACTED]`` and its
    row index is returned in the second list. Other values in that row are
    still replaced.
    """
    extracted = self.ner.extract(inputs, entity_type=entity)[entity]
    if entity == "Name":
        self.entity_mapping, self.entity_lookup = self.encrypt_names(extracted, use_fpe=use_fpe)
    elif entity == "Money":
        if not (use_fpe or use_mdp):
            raise ValueError("Money needs use_fpe or use_mdp to be True.")
        self.entity_mapping = self.encrypt_money(extracted, use_fpe=use_fpe, epsilon=epsilon)
    elif entity == "Age":
        self.entity_mapping = self.encrypt_age(extracted, epsilon=epsilon)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown entity: {entity!r}")

    sanitized, invalid = [], []
    for i, (line, fakes) in enumerate(zip(inputs, self.entity_mapping)):
        replaced = line
        failed = False
        for original, fake in fakes.items():
            if fake is None:
                failed = True
                replaced = _nfc(replaced).replace(_nfc(original), REDACTED)
                continue
            replaced = _nfc(replaced).replace(_nfc(original), fake)
        if failed:
            invalid.append(i)
        sanitized.append(replaced)
    return sanitized, invalid

def encrypt_names(
    self, inputs: list[list[str]], use_fpe: bool = True
) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Optional[str]]], list[dict[str, str]]]:
    """Map each name to a fake name, per text.

    With FPE, each word is swapped on its own (first word in the first-name
    list, later words in the last-name list), so "Sarah Lopez", "Sarah" and
    "Lopez" map consistently, within and across calls. Without FPE, fake
    names are random and can't be decrypted.

    Returns ``{original: fake}`` per text and, per text, the
    ``{fake word: original word}`` entries for words outside the lists.
    """
    if not use_fpe:
        mappings: list[dict[str, Optional[str]]] = []
        for text_names in inputs:
            fakes: dict[str, Optional[str]] = {}
            for name in text_names:
                fakes.setdefault(name, names.get_full_name(gender="male"))
            mappings.append(fakes)
        return mappings, [{} for _ in inputs]

    self._load_name_lists()
    mappings, fallbacks = [], []
    for text_names in inputs:
        roles = self._word_roles(text_names)
        word_fakes = {w: self._permute_word(w, role) for w, role in roles.items() if w in self._name_index[role]}
        # Unlisted words get a keyed pick that avoids surrogates used here.
        used = set(word_fakes.values())
        fallback: dict[str, str] = {}
        for word, role in roles.items():
            if word not in word_fakes:
                fake = self._fallback_word(word, role, used)
                word_fakes[word] = fake
                fallback[fake] = word
                used.add(fake)

        fakes = {}
        for name in text_names:
            fakes.setdefault(name, " ".join(word_fakes[w] for w in _nfc(name).split()))
        for word, fake in word_fakes.items():
            fakes.setdefault(word, fake)
        mappings.append(fakes)
        fallbacks.append(fallback)
    return mappings, fallbacks

    spans : list[tuple[int, int, str]]
        ``(start, end, label)`` character spans. Spans must not overlap.

    Returns
    -------
    list[int]
        Tag id per token. Empty offsets are ``-100``.

    """
    tags: list[int] = []
    active: tuple[int, int, str] | None = None
    for token_start, token_end in offset_mapping:
        if token_start == token_end:
            tags.append(IGNORE_TAG_ID)
            continue
        matches = [span for span in spans if span[0] <= token_start < span[1]]
        if len(matches) > 1:
            raise ValueError(f"overlapping spans at offset {token_start}")
        if not matches:
            tags.append(TAG_TO_ID["O"])
            active = None
            continue
        start, end, label = matches[0]
        tag_name = f"I-{label}" if active == (start, end, label) else f"B-{label}"
        if tag_name not in TAG_TO_ID:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown label: {label}")
        tags.append(TAG_TO_ID[tag_name])
        active = (start, end, label)
    return tags

def spans_from_tags(
    text: str,
    offset_mapping: list[tuple[int, int]],
    tag_ids: list[int],
    confidences: list[float],
    source: str,
) -> tuple[list[EntitySpan], int]:
    """Decode BIO tags into character spans.

    An ``I-`` tag with no open span of the same label is counted and dropped.
    Spans whose slice does not match the source text are counted and dropped.

    Parameters
    ----------
    text : str
        Original text.
    offset_mapping : list[tuple[int, int]]
        ``(start, end)`` character offsets for each token.
    tag_ids : list[int]
        BIO tag id per token.
    confidences : list[float]
        Score per token, parallel to ``tag_ids``.
    source : str
        Value stored on each emitted span.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[list[EntitySpan], int]
        Accepted spans, and how many tag pieces were dropped.

    """
    if not (len(offset_mapping) == len(tag_ids) == len(confidences)):
        raise ValueError("offsets, tags, and confidences differ in length")

    spans: list[EntitySpan] = []
    dropped = 0
    open_label: str | None = None
    open_start = 0
    open_end = 0
    open_scores: list[float] = []

    def close() -> None:
        nonlocal dropped, open_label
        if open_label is None:
            return
        label = open_label
        start = open_start
        end = open_end
        scores = list(open_scores)
        open_label = None
        open_scores.clear()
        if start >= end or not scores:
            dropped += 1
            return
        span = EntitySpan(
            start=start,
            end=end,
            text=text[start:end],
            label=label,
            confidence=min(scores),
            source=source,
        )
        try:
            validate_span(text, span)
        except ValueError:
            dropped += 1
        else:
            spans.append(span)

    for (token_start, token_end), tag_id, score in zip(
        offset_mapping,
        tag_ids,
        confidences,
        strict=True,
    ):
        if token_start == token_end or tag_id == IGNORE_TAG_ID:
            continue
        tag = ID_TO_TAG[tag_id]
        if tag == "O":
            close()
            continue
        prefix, label = tag.split("-", 1)
        if prefix == "I" and open_label == label:
            open_end = token_end
            open_scores.append(score)
            continue
        if prefix == "I":
            close()
            dropped += 1
            continue
        close()
        open_label = label
        open_start = token_start
        open_end = token_end
        open_scores = [score]

    close()
    return spans, dropped

    """Raise ValueError when the span does not match the source text.

        raise ValueError(f"span offsets out of range: {span.start}:{span.end}")

class DistilBertRecognizer:
    """Load a fine-tuned DistilBERT checkpoint and emit character spans.

    The ONNX backend runs an exported graph with onnxruntime. The PyTorch
    backend needs the ``torch`` extra.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        model_path: str,
        max_length: int = 512,
        backend: Literal["pytorch", "onnx"] = "pytorch",
        onnx_file_name: str | None = None,
        stride: int = 128,
    ) -> None:
        """Load the tokenizer and token-classification head.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model_path : str
            Hugging Face model id or a local checkpoint directory.
        max_length : int
            Maximum tokens per window, including special tokens. Longer text
            is read in overlapping windows rather than truncated.
        backend : Literal["pytorch", "onnx"]
            Backend to use for inference. ``onnx`` reads an exported graph
            and does not import PyTorch.
        onnx_file_name : str | None
            ONNX file to load from ``model_path``, such as ``model.onnx`` or
            ``model.int8.onnx``. Required only when the directory contains
            multiple ONNX model variants.
        stride : int
            Content tokens repeated from the previous window. An entity longer
            than this can still be split.

        Raises
        ------
        ImportError
            ``backend`` is ``pytorch`` and the ``torch`` extra is not installed.
        ValueError
            ``stride`` leaves the window with no room to move forward.

        """
        if backend not in ("pytorch", "onnx"):
            raise ValueError(f"unknown backend: {backend}")
        if stride < 0:
            raise ValueError("stride must be >= 0")
        self.backend: Literal["pytorch", "onnx"] = backend
        self.max_length = max_length
        self.stride = stride
        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path, use_fast=True)
        special = self.tokenizer.num_special_tokens_to_add(pair=False)
        if self.max_length - special <= self.stride:
            raise ValueError(
                "stride must be smaller than max_length minus the tokenizer's special tokens, "
                "so each window moves forward"
            )
        self.config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(model_path)
        if backend == "pytorch":
            if onnx_file_name is not None:
                raise ValueError("onnx_file_name can only be used with the ONNX backend")
            torch = _require_torch()
            from transformers import AutoModelForTokenClassification  # noqa: PLC0415

            self.model = AutoModelForTokenClassification.from_pretrained(model_path)
            self.model.eval()
            self._torch = torch
            self.session = None
        else:
            onnx_file = _onnx_file(model_path, onnx_file_name)
            self.session = ort.InferenceSession(onnx_file, providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])
            self.model = None
            self._torch = None
        self._check_labels()

    def _check_labels(self) -> None:
        raw = self.config.id2label
        actual = {int(key): str(value) for key, value in raw.items()}
        if actual != ID_TO_TAG:
            raise ValueError("checkpoint labels do not match the BIO label set")

    def recognize(self, text: str) -> list[EntitySpan]:
        """Return PII spans in ``text``.

        Text longer than ``max_length`` is read in overlapping windows. Spans
        from those windows are merged, keeping the longer span when the same
        label overlaps.

        Parameters
        ----------
        text : str
            Source text.

        Returns
        -------
        list[EntitySpan]
            Spans sliced from ``text``. ``source`` is ``distilbert``.

        """
        windows = token_windows(self.tokenizer, text, self.max_length, self.stride)
        normalized: list[EntitySpan] = []
        for char_start, char_end in windows:
            normalized.extend(self._spans_in_window(text, char_start, char_end))
        if len(windows) > 1:
            normalized = merge_overlapping_spans(normalized)
        # The checkpoint tags many "$10,000" style amounts as O, or as an ID
        # that covers only the digits before the comma. A symbol-led amount
        # fills that gap unless a MONEY span already covers it.
        for start, end in currency_spans(text):
            if any(span.label == "MONEY" and span.start <= start and span.end >= end for span in normalized):
                continue
            normalized = [
                span for span in normalized if not (span.label == "MONEY" and span.start < end and start < span.end)
            ]
            normalized.append(
                EntitySpan(
                    start=start,
                    end=end,
                    text=text[start:end],
                    label="MONEY",
                    confidence=1.0,
                    source="currency",
                )
            )
        normalized.sort(key=lambda span: (span.start, span.end))
        return normalized

    def _spans_in_window(self, text: str, char_start: int, char_end: int) -> list[EntitySpan]:
        """Run one window and return spans in the coordinates of ``text``."""
        encoded = self.tokenizer(
            text[char_start:char_end],
            return_offsets_mapping=True,
            truncation=True,
            max_length=self.max_length,
            return_tensors="np",
        )
        # pop offset_mapping from the encoded dictionary because model doesn't accept it
        # [0] selects first batch item.
        # offset_mapping is [batch_size, tokens, 2], where the last axis is
        # the character start and end of the window. Shift it onto ``text``.
        offset_rows = encoded.pop("offset_mapping")[0].tolist()
        offsets = _shift_offsets([(int(start), int(end)) for start, end in offset_rows], char_start)
        logits = self._onnx_logits(encoded) if self.backend == "onnx" else self._pytorch_logits(encoded)
        # probs is [tokens, num_labels]
        probs = _softmax(logits)
        # tag_ids is [tokens]
        tag_ids = [int(tag_id) for tag_id in probs.argmax(axis=-1).tolist()]
        # confidences is [tokens]
        confidences = [float(score) for score in probs.max(axis=-1).tolist()]
        spans, _dropped = spans_from_tags(text, offsets, tag_ids, confidences, source="distilbert")
        # Snap AGE to its digits and MONEY to the full amount, same as training eval.
        # NAME and the other labels keep the decoded bounds.
        normalized: list[EntitySpan] = []
        for span in spans:
            start, end = normalize_span(text, span.start, span.end, span.label)
            if start >= end:
                start, end = span.start, span.end
            normalized.append(
                EntitySpan(
                    start=start,
                    end=end,
                    text=text[start:end],
                    label=span.label,
                    confidence=span.confidence,
                    source=span.source,
                )
            )
        return normalized

    def _onnx_logits(self, encoded: Mapping[str, np.ndarray]) -> np.ndarray:
        if self.session is None:
            raise RuntimeError("ONNX session is not loaded")
        feeds: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        for item in self.session.get_inputs():
            if item.name not in encoded:
                raise ValueError(f"tokenizer did not produce ONNX input {item.name}")
            value = encoded[item.name]
            if value.dtype.kind in "iu":
                value = value.astype(np.int64)
            feeds[item.name] = value
        outputs = self.session.run(["logits"], feeds)
        # logits is [batch_size, tokens, num_tags]. [0] drops the batch axis.
        return np.asarray(outputs[0][0])

    def _pytorch_logits(self, encoded: Mapping[str, np.ndarray]) -> np.ndarray:
        torch = self._torch if self._torch is not None else _require_torch()
        if self.model is None:
            raise RuntimeError("PyTorch model is not loaded")
        batch = {name: torch.from_numpy(value) for name, value in encoded.items()}
        with torch.no_grad():
            logits = self.model(**batch).logits[0]
        return logits.detach().cpu().numpy()

def token_windows(tokenizer: Any, text: str, max_length: int, stride: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Return character slices that cover ``text`` without passing ``max_length``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    tokenizer : Any
        Fast tokenizer. Used for offsets and the special-token count.
    text : str
        Source text.
    max_length : int
        Maximum tokens per window, including special tokens.
    stride : int
        Content tokens repeated from the previous window.

    Returns
    -------
    list[tuple[int, int]]
        ``(start, end)`` slices of ``text``. A text that fits is one slice.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        The text is longer than ``max_length`` and the tokenizer returned no
        character offsets, so the tail cannot be scanned.

    """
    encoded = tokenizer(
        text,
        add_special_tokens=False,
        return_offsets_mapping=True,
        truncation=False,
    )
    raw_offsets = encoded["offset_mapping"]
    ids = encoded["input_ids"]
    offsets = [(int(start), int(end)) for start, end in raw_offsets if int(start) != int(end)]
    special = tokenizer.num_special_tokens_to_add(pair=False)
    if not offsets and len(ids) + special > max_length:
        raise ValueError(
            "text is longer than max_length and the tokenizer returned no character offsets, "
            "so it cannot be scanned in windows"
        )
    return covering_windows(offsets, size=max_length - special, overlap=stride, text_length=len(text))

class GlinerRecognizer:
    """Load a zero-shot GLiNER checkpoint and emit character spans."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        model_path: str = DEFAULT_MODEL_ID,
        threshold: float = 0.5,
        labels: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
        overlap: int = 32,
    ) -> None:
        """Load the model and the label prompts it will score.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model_path : str
            Hugging Face model id or a local checkpoint directory.
        threshold : float
            Minimum score for a span to be kept.
        labels : Mapping[str, str] | None
            Pipeline label to prompt text. Defaults to ``LABEL_PROMPTS``.
            Prompt strings must be unique. Returned spans use the keys.
        overlap : int
            Words repeated from the previous window when the text is longer
            than the model's ``max_len``. An entity longer than this can still
            be split.

        Raises
        ------
        ImportError
            The ``gliner`` extra is not installed.
        ValueError
            ``overlap`` is negative.

        """
        if overlap < 0:
            raise ValueError("overlap must be >= 0")
        self.threshold = threshold
        self.overlap = overlap
        self.labels = _check_labels(LABEL_PROMPTS if labels is None else labels)
        # Imported here so an install without the gliner extra does not need it.
        try:
            from gliner import GLiNER  # noqa: PLC0415
        except ImportError as exc:
            raise ImportError("GlinerRecognizer requires the gliner extra: uv sync --extra gliner") from exc
        self.model = GLiNER.from_pretrained(model_path)
        self.model.eval()

    def recognize(self, text: str) -> list[EntitySpan]:
        """Return PII spans in ``text``.

        Text longer than the model's ``max_len`` is read in overlapping word
        windows. GLiNER would otherwise truncate and leave the tail unscanned.

        Parameters
        ----------
        text : str
            Source text.

        Returns
        -------
        list[EntitySpan]
            Spans sliced from ``text``. ``source`` is ``gliner``.
            Overlapping spans are dropped (flat NER).

        """
        if not text:
            return []
        windows = self._windows(text)
        spans: list[EntitySpan] = []
        for char_start, char_end in windows:
            spans.extend(self._spans_in_window(text, char_start, char_end))
        if len(windows) > 1:
            spans = merge_overlapping_spans(spans)
        spans.sort(key=lambda span: (span.start, span.end))
        return spans

    def _windows(self, text: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        """Character slices that stay within the model's word limit."""
        max_words = int(getattr(self.model.config, "max_len", 0) or 0)
        processor = getattr(self.model, "data_processor", None)
        splitter = getattr(processor, "words_splitter", None)
        if max_words < 1 or splitter is None:
            return [(0, len(text))]
        words = [(int(start), int(end)) for _token, start, end in splitter(text) if int(start) != int(end)]
        overlap = min(self.overlap, max_words - 1)
        return covering_windows(words, size=max_words, overlap=overlap, text_length=len(text))

    def _spans_in_window(self, text: str, char_start: int, char_end: int) -> list[EntitySpan]:
        """Score one slice and return spans in the coordinates of ``text``."""
        chunk = text[char_start:char_end]
        if not chunk:
            return []
        entities = self.model.predict_entities(
            chunk,
            self.labels,
            flat_ner=True,
            threshold=self.threshold,
        )
        spans: list[EntitySpan] = []
        for entity in entities:
            label = str(entity["label"])
            if label not in self.labels:
                raise ValueError(f"unknown label: {label}")
            start = int(entity["start"]) + char_start
            end = int(entity["end"]) + char_start
            if start < 0 or end > len(text) or start >= end:
                continue
            spans.append(
                EntitySpan(
                    start=start,
                    end=end,
                    text=text[start:end],
                    label=label,
                    confidence=float(entity["score"]),
                    source="gliner",
                )
            )
        return spans

    model_path: str = DEFAULT_MODEL_ID,
    threshold: float = 0.5,
    labels: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,

) -> None:
    """Load the model and the label prompts it will score.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model_path : str
        Hugging Face model id or a local checkpoint directory.
    threshold : float
        Minimum score for a span to be kept.
    labels : Mapping[str, str] | None

        than the model's ``max_len``. An entity longer than this can still
        be split.

    Raises
    ------
    ImportError
        The ``gliner`` extra is not installed.
    ValueError
        ``overlap`` is negative.

    """
    if overlap < 0:
        raise ValueError("overlap must be >= 0")
    self.threshold = threshold
    self.overlap = overlap
    self.labels = _check_labels(LABEL_PROMPTS if labels is None else labels)
    # Imported here so an install without the gliner extra does not need it.
    try:
        from gliner import GLiNER  # noqa: PLC0415
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise ImportError("GlinerRecognizer requires the gliner extra: uv sync --extra gliner") from exc
    self.model = GLiNER.from_pretrained(model_path)
    self.model.eval()

def recognize(self, text: str) -> list[EntitySpan]:
    """Return PII spans in ``text``.

    Text longer than the model's ``max_len`` is read in overlapping word
    windows. GLiNER would otherwise truncate and leave the tail unscanned.

    Parameters
    ----------
    text : str
        Source text.

    Returns
    -------
    list[EntitySpan]
        Spans sliced from ``text``. ``source`` is ``gliner``.
        Overlapping spans are dropped (flat NER).

    """
    if not text:
        return []
    windows = self._windows(text)
    spans: list[EntitySpan] = []
    for char_start, char_end in windows:
        spans.extend(self._spans_in_window(text, char_start, char_end))
    if len(windows) > 1:
        spans = merge_overlapping_spans(spans)
    spans.sort(key=lambda span: (span.start, span.end))
    return spans

Replace names, money, and ages in text with fake values, and undo it.

  • Names: a keyed permutation of fixed first- and last-name lists (reversible with the key alone), or random names. Words outside the lists get a keyed hash pick that only the encrypt call's saved state can reverse.
  • Money: FPE (reversible) or m-LDP noise. FPE appends a non-zero suffix so a round amount does not make FF3 reject the value.
  • Ages: m-LDP noise.

decrypt restores only the surrogates saved by the last encrypt call on this instance. key_only=True inverts listed names and FPE amounts with the key alone. A value that cannot be encrypted is replaced with [REDACTED]; the other values in that text are still replaced.

Known limitation: values are matched as plain substrings ("Ann" also hits "Anna"), and some decrypt paths restore only the first match. See https://github.com/VectorInstitute/preempt-guardrail/issues/11.

class Sanitizer:
    """Encrypt and decrypt names, money, and ages detected by ``ner_model``."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        ner_model: Any,
        key: str,
        tweak: str,
        seed: Optional[int] = None,
    ):
        """Set up the FF3 cipher and name permutations for ``key`` and ``tweak``.

        Anyone with ``key`` and ``tweak`` can reverse FPE names and amounts,
        so keep them secret. Use ``generate_key`` to make a fresh pair.
        ``ner_model`` is either an object with ``extract`` or a ``Recognizer``,
        which is wrapped in ``LegacyNERShim``.
        """
        self.cipher_fn = FF3Cipher(key, tweak, allow_small_domain=True, radix=10)
        self._key, self._tweak = key, tweak
        if hasattr(ner_model, "recognize") and not hasattr(ner_model, "extract"):
            ner_model = LegacyNERShim(ner_model)
        self.ner = ner_model
        # Set by encrypt(), read by decrypt().
        self.entity_mapping: list[dict[str, Optional[str]]] = []  # {original: fake} per text
        # {fake word: original word} per text, for name words outside the fixed lists.
        self.entity_lookup: list[dict[str, str]] = []
        self._names_dataset: Optional[dict[str, list[str]]] = None
        self._name_lists: dict[str, list[str]] = {}  # {"first" | "last": names}
        self._name_index: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
        self._name_perm: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        self._name_inverse: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        self.reseed(seed)

    def reseed(self, seed: Optional[int]) -> None:
        """Reset the RNGs used by m-LDP noise and random names."""
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        if seed is not None:
            random.seed(seed)

    # --- Public API -----------------------------------------------------------

    def encrypt(
        self, inputs: list[str], epsilon: float = 0.1, entity: str = "Name", use_mdp: bool = False, use_fpe: bool = True
    ) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:
        """Replace every detected ``entity`` ("Name", "Money", or "Age") in ``inputs``.

        A value that cannot be encrypted is replaced with ``[REDACTED]`` and its
        row index is returned in the second list. Other values in that row are
        still replaced.
        """
        extracted = self.ner.extract(inputs, entity_type=entity)[entity]
        if entity == "Name":
            self.entity_mapping, self.entity_lookup = self.encrypt_names(extracted, use_fpe=use_fpe)
        elif entity == "Money":
            if not (use_fpe or use_mdp):
                raise ValueError("Money needs use_fpe or use_mdp to be True.")
            self.entity_mapping = self.encrypt_money(extracted, use_fpe=use_fpe, epsilon=epsilon)
        elif entity == "Age":
            self.entity_mapping = self.encrypt_age(extracted, epsilon=epsilon)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown entity: {entity!r}")

        sanitized, invalid = [], []
        for i, (line, fakes) in enumerate(zip(inputs, self.entity_mapping)):
            replaced = line
            failed = False
            for original, fake in fakes.items():
                if fake is None:
                    failed = True
                    replaced = _nfc(replaced).replace(_nfc(original), REDACTED)
                    continue
                replaced = _nfc(replaced).replace(_nfc(original), fake)
            if failed:
                invalid.append(i)
            sanitized.append(replaced)
        return sanitized, invalid

    def decrypt(  # noqa: PLR0917
        self,
        inputs: list[str],
        entity: str = "Name",
        extracted: Optional[list[list[str]]] = None,
        use_mdp: bool = False,  # noqa: ARG002 -- kept for API compatibility; m-LDP is used when not use_fpe
        use_fpe: bool = True,
        use_cache: bool = False,  # noqa: ARG002 -- stateful decrypt always uses saved surrogates
        key_only: bool = False,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Restore values that ``encrypt`` replaced.

        By default only surrogates saved by the last ``encrypt`` call on this
        instance are restored. A name or amount that was never encrypted is
        left as it is, including one the recognizer missed and one added later.

        Pass ``key_only=True`` to invert listed names and FPE amounts with the
        key alone. Targets then come from ``extracted``, or from a fresh
        recognizer pass when ``extracted`` is omitted. An amount FF3 rejects
        is left in place. Ages have no key-only inverse; they still use the
        saved state.

        ``use_cache`` is accepted for existing callers. Stateful decrypt always
        uses the saved surrogates.
        """
        if key_only and extracted is None and entity != "Age":
            extracted = self.ner.extract(inputs, entity_type=entity)[entity]
        if entity == "Name":
            return self.decrypt_names(inputs, extracted, key_only=key_only)
        if entity == "Money":
            return self.decrypt_money(inputs, extracted, use_fpe=use_fpe, key_only=key_only)
        if entity == "Age":
            return self.decrypt_age(inputs)
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown entity: {entity!r}")

    # --- Names ----------------------------------------------------------------

    def encrypt_names(
        self, inputs: list[list[str]], use_fpe: bool = True
    ) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Optional[str]]], list[dict[str, str]]]:
        """Map each name to a fake name, per text.

        With FPE, each word is swapped on its own (first word in the first-name
        list, later words in the last-name list), so "Sarah Lopez", "Sarah" and
        "Lopez" map consistently, within and across calls. Without FPE, fake
        names are random and can't be decrypted.

        Returns ``{original: fake}`` per text and, per text, the
        ``{fake word: original word}`` entries for words outside the lists.
        """
        if not use_fpe:
            mappings: list[dict[str, Optional[str]]] = []
            for text_names in inputs:
                fakes: dict[str, Optional[str]] = {}
                for name in text_names:
                    fakes.setdefault(name, names.get_full_name(gender="male"))
                mappings.append(fakes)
            return mappings, [{} for _ in inputs]

        self._load_name_lists()
        mappings, fallbacks = [], []
        for text_names in inputs:
            roles = self._word_roles(text_names)
            word_fakes = {w: self._permute_word(w, role) for w, role in roles.items() if w in self._name_index[role]}
            # Unlisted words get a keyed pick that avoids surrogates used here.
            used = set(word_fakes.values())
            fallback: dict[str, str] = {}
            for word, role in roles.items():
                if word not in word_fakes:
                    fake = self._fallback_word(word, role, used)
                    word_fakes[word] = fake
                    fallback[fake] = word
                    used.add(fake)

            fakes = {}
            for name in text_names:
                fakes.setdefault(name, " ".join(word_fakes[w] for w in _nfc(name).split()))
            for word, fake in word_fakes.items():
                fakes.setdefault(word, fake)
            mappings.append(fakes)
            fallbacks.append(fallback)
        return mappings, fallbacks

    def decrypt_names(
        self,
        inputs: list[str],
        extracted: Optional[list[list[str]]],
        use_cache: bool = False,  # noqa: ARG002 -- stateful decrypt always uses saved surrogates
        key_only: bool = False,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Replace fake names in ``inputs`` with the originals.

        By default only surrogates from the last ``encrypt`` call are undone.
        ``key_only=True`` inverts every target with the key. Words from the
        fixed lists need only the key; words that were outside the lists need
        the state saved by ``encrypt``. Words that are neither are left as
        they are.
        """
        self._load_name_lists()
        decrypted = []
        for i, line in enumerate(inputs):
            fallback = self.entity_lookup[i] if i < len(self.entity_lookup) else {}
            restored = line
            for fake in self._decrypt_targets(i, extracted, key_only):
                restored = restored.replace(fake, self._decrypt_name(fake, fallback))
            decrypted.append(restored)
        return decrypted

    def _decrypt_name(self, fake: str, fallback: dict[str, str]) -> str:
        """Undo the word swaps in one fake name."""
        words = _nfc(fake).split()
        if len(words) == 1:
            # The lists share no names, so a lone word's list is unambiguous.
            roles = ["first" if words[0] in self._name_index["first"] else "last"]
        else:
            roles = ["first"] + ["last"] * (len(words) - 1)
        restored = []
        for word, role in zip(words, roles):
            if word in fallback:
                restored.append(fallback[word])
            elif (i := self._name_index[role].get(word)) is not None:
                restored.append(self._name_lists[role][self._name_inverse[role][i]])
            else:
                restored.append(word)
        return " ".join(restored)

    def _word_roles(self, text_names: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Assign each name word to the "first" or "last" list, once per text."""
        later_words = {w for name in text_names for w in _nfc(name).split()[1:]}
        roles: dict[str, str] = {}
        for name in text_names:
            words = _nfc(name).split()
            for pos, word in enumerate(words):
                if word in roles:
                    continue
                if len(words) > 1:
                    roles[word] = "first" if pos == 0 else "last"
                elif word in later_words or (
                    word in self._name_index["last"] and word not in self._name_index["first"]
                ):
                    roles[word] = "last"
                else:
                    roles[word] = "first"
        return roles

    def _permute_word(self, word: str, role: str) -> str:
        return self._name_lists[role][self._name_perm[role][self._name_index[role][word]]]

    def _fallback_word(self, word: str, role: str, used: set[str]) -> str:
        """Pick a list name for an unlisted word by keyed hash, skipping ``used``."""
        names_list = self._name_lists[role]
        for attempt in itertools.count():
            digest = hashlib.sha256(f"{self._key}:{self._tweak}:{role}:{word}:{attempt}".encode()).digest()
            fake = names_list[int.from_bytes(digest[:8], "big") % len(names_list)]
            if fake not in used:
                return fake
        raise AssertionError("unreachable")

    def _load_name_lists(self) -> None:
        """Build the fixed first/last name lists and their keyed permutations once.

        The lists depend only on the names dataset, never on the inputs, so a
        name's surrogate depends only on the name and the key. The last-name
        list excludes every first name, so the two lists share no names.
        """
        if self._name_lists:
            return
        dataset = self._load_names_dataset()
        first = _clean_names(dataset["first_names"], exclude=set())
        last = _clean_names(dataset["last_names"], exclude=set(first))
        if len(first) < ALPHABET_SIZE or len(last) < ALPHABET_SIZE:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Names dataset has {len(first)} first and {len(last)} last names; need {ALPHABET_SIZE} of each."
            )
        for role, names_list in (("first", first[:ALPHABET_SIZE]), ("last", last[:ALPHABET_SIZE])):
            seed = int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(f"{self._key}:{self._tweak}:{role}".encode()).digest()[:8], "big")
            perm = np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation(ALPHABET_SIZE)
            self._name_lists[role] = names_list
            self._name_index[role] = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(names_list)}
            self._name_perm[role] = perm
            self._name_inverse[role] = np.argsort(perm)

    def _load_names_dataset(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """Load the dataset of first and last names once, generating it if missing."""
        if self._names_dataset is not None:
            return self._names_dataset
        candidates = [
            os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "names_dataset.json"),
            "preempt/names_dataset.json",
            f"{os.getcwd()}/names_dataset.json",
        ]
        path = next((p for p in candidates if os.path.exists(p)), None)
        if path is None:
            path = candidates[-1]
            logger.info("Names dataset not found. Generating %s", path)
            make_names_dataset(path)
        self._names_dataset = load_data(path)
        return self._names_dataset

    # --- Money ----------------------------------------------------------------

    def encrypt_money(
        self, inputs: list[list[str]], use_fpe: bool = True, epsilon: Optional[float] = None
    ) -> list[dict[str, Optional[str]]]:
        """Map each amount to an FPE-encrypted or m-LDP-noised amount, per text.

        Amounts that can't be parsed map to None.
        """
        mappings = []
        for amounts in inputs:
            fakes: dict[str, Optional[str]] = {}
            for amount in amounts:
                if amount in fakes:
                    continue
                digits = amount.replace(",", "")
                try:
                    if use_fpe:
                        fakes[amount] = self.fpe_encrypt(digits + MONEY_FPE_SUFFIX)
                    else:
                        value = int(float(digits))
                        fakes[amount] = str(self.m_epsilon(value, *_money_bounds(value), epsilon))
                except (ValueError, TypeError):
                    fakes[amount] = None
            mappings.append(fakes)
        return mappings

    def decrypt_money(
        self,
        inputs: list[str],
        extracted: Optional[list[list[str]]],
        use_fpe: bool = True,
        use_cache: bool = False,  # noqa: ARG002 -- stateful decrypt always uses saved surrogates
        key_only: bool = False,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Replace fake amounts in ``inputs`` with the originals.

        By default only surrogates from the last ``encrypt`` call are undone.
        ``key_only=True`` inverts FPE amounts with the key and skips a value
        FF3 rejects, so one amount cannot fail the batch.
        """
        decrypted = []
        for i, line in enumerate(inputs):
            restored = line
            mapping = self.entity_mapping[i] if i < len(self.entity_mapping) else {}
            fake_to_original = {fake: original for original, fake in mapping.items() if fake is not None}
            for fake in self._decrypt_targets(i, extracted, key_only):
                if not use_fpe:
                    original = fake_to_original.get(fake)
                    if original is None:
                        continue
                    restored = _replace_first_word(restored, fake, original)
                    continue
                original = self._unwrap_money(fake)
                if original is None:
                    continue
                if fake in restored:
                    restored = restored.replace(fake, original)
                else:  # e.g. "1.250" was written as "1,250"
                    restored = restored.replace(fake.replace(".", ","), original.replace(".", ","))
            decrypted.append(restored)
        return decrypted

    # --- Age ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def encrypt_age(self, inputs: list[list[str]], epsilon: Optional[float] = None) -> list[dict[str, Optional[str]]]:
        """Map each age to an m-LDP-noised age in [10, 99], per text.

        Ages that can't be parsed map to None.
        """
        mappings = []
        for ages in inputs:
            fakes: dict[str, Optional[str]] = {}
            for age in ages:
                if age in fakes:
                    continue
                try:
                    fakes[age] = str(self.m_epsilon(int(age), 10, 99, epsilon))
                except (ValueError, TypeError):
                    fakes[age] = None
            mappings.append(fakes)
        return mappings

    def decrypt_age(self, inputs: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        """Restore ages saved by the last ``encrypt`` call."""
        decrypted = []
        for line, fakes in zip(inputs, self.entity_mapping):
            restored = line
            for original, fake in fakes.items():
                if fake is not None:
                    restored = _replace_first_word(restored, fake, original)
            decrypted.append(restored)
        return decrypted

    # --- Building blocks ------------------------------------------------------

    def fpe_encrypt(self, value: str) -> str:
        """FPE-encrypt the digits of ``value``, keeping its punctuation."""
        return _restore_format(self.cipher_fn.encrypt(_digits_only(value)), str(value))

    def fpe_decrypt(self, value: str) -> str:
        """Undo ``fpe_encrypt``."""
        return _restore_format(self.cipher_fn.decrypt(_digits_only(value)), str(value))

    def m_epsilon(self, x: int, n_lower: int, n_upper: int, epsilon: float, discretization_size: int = 100) -> int:
        """Noise ``x`` with m-LDP: sample near ``x`` within [n_lower, n_upper].

        Smaller ``epsilon`` means more noise.
        """
        n_lower, n_upper = int(n_lower), int(n_upper)
        total_range = n_upper - n_lower
        x_scaled = (x - n_lower) * discretization_size / total_range
        p = np.exp(-np.abs(x_scaled - np.arange(discretization_size)) * epsilon / 2)
        sample = self.rng.choice(discretization_size, 1, p=p / p.sum())[0]
        return int(sample * total_range / discretization_size + n_lower)

    def _unwrap_money(self, fake: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """Return the original digits of an FPE amount.

        ``None`` when ``fake`` is too short to be one of ours, FF3 rejects it,
        or decrypting it does not end in the suffix this class appends.
        """
        if len(_digits_only(fake)) <= len(MONEY_FPE_SUFFIX):
            return None
        try:
            decoded = self.fpe_decrypt(fake)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            return None
        if not decoded.endswith(MONEY_FPE_SUFFIX):
            return None
        return decoded[: -len(MONEY_FPE_SUFFIX)]

    def _saved_fakes(self, index: int) -> list[str]:
        """Surrogates saved by ``encrypt`` for text ``index``, in insertion order."""
        if index >= len(self.entity_mapping):
            return []
        return [fake for fake in dict.fromkeys(self.entity_mapping[index].values()) if fake is not None]

    def _decrypt_targets(self, index: int, extracted: Optional[list[list[str]]], key_only: bool) -> list[str]:
        """Values to undo in text ``index``.

        Stateful decrypt uses the surrogates ``encrypt`` saved. Key-only
        decrypt uses ``extracted`` and does not require that call.
        """
        if not key_only:
            return self._saved_fakes(index)
        if extracted is None:
            return []
        return list(extracted[index])

    self,
    ner_model: Any,
    key: str,
    tweak: str,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
):
    """Set up the FF3 cipher and name permutations for ``key`` and ``tweak``.

    Anyone with ``key`` and ``tweak`` can reverse FPE names and amounts,
    so keep them secret. Use ``generate_key`` to make a fresh pair.

def encrypt(
    self, inputs: list[str], epsilon: float = 0.1, entity: str = "Name", use_mdp: bool = False, use_fpe: bool = True
) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:
    """Replace every detected ``entity`` ("Name", "Money", or "Age") in ``inputs``.

    A value that cannot be encrypted is replaced with ``[REDACTED]`` and its
    row index is returned in the second list. Other values in that row are
    still replaced.
    """
    extracted = self.ner.extract(inputs, entity_type=entity)[entity]
    if entity == "Name":
        self.entity_mapping, self.entity_lookup = self.encrypt_names(extracted, use_fpe=use_fpe)
    elif entity == "Money":
        if not (use_fpe or use_mdp):
            raise ValueError("Money needs use_fpe or use_mdp to be True.")
        self.entity_mapping = self.encrypt_money(extracted, use_fpe=use_fpe, epsilon=epsilon)
    elif entity == "Age":
        self.entity_mapping = self.encrypt_age(extracted, epsilon=epsilon)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown entity: {entity!r}")

    sanitized, invalid = [], []
    for i, (line, fakes) in enumerate(zip(inputs, self.entity_mapping)):
        replaced = line
        failed = False
        for original, fake in fakes.items():
            if fake is None:
                failed = True
                replaced = _nfc(replaced).replace(_nfc(original), REDACTED)
                continue
            replaced = _nfc(replaced).replace(_nfc(original), fake)
        if failed:
            invalid.append(i)
        sanitized.append(replaced)
    return sanitized, invalid
